{{Short description|Results in differential topology}}
In [[differential topology]] in mathematics, the '''Wall theorems''' are four results, which connect the [[smooth structure]], auto-[[Diffeomorphism|diffeomorphisms]] and the [[Intersection form of a 4-manifold|intersection form]] of a smooth [[4-manifold]] with [[H-cobordism|h-cobordisms]], stable diffeomorphisms and induced form automorphisms. The theorems are named after [[C. T. C. Wall]], who proved them in 1964.

== Wall's theorem on h-cobordisms ==
'''Wall's theorem on h-cobordisms''' claims, that [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] closed smooth 4-manifolds with isomorphic [[intersection form]] are even [[H-cobordism|h-cobordant]].<ref>Wall 1964 (''On simply-connected 4-manifolds''), Thrm. 2</ref><ref>Scorpan 05, p. 155</ref>

== Wall's theorem on stabilization ==
'''Wall's theorem on stabilization''' claims, that for h-cobordant simply connected closed smooth 4-manifolds <math>M</math> and <math>N</math>, there exists a natural number <math>n\in\mathbb{N}</math> and a [[diffeomorphism]] <math>M\#n(S^2\times S^2)\cong N\#n(S^2\times S^2)</math>.<ref>Wall 1964 (''On simply-connected 4-manifolds''), Thrm. 3</ref><ref>Scorpan 05, p. 149</ref> Becoming diffeomorphic after [[Connected sum|connected sums]] with <math>S^2\times S^2</math> is also called stably diffeomorphic. A combination with Wall's theorem on h-cobordisms yields that simply connected smooth 4-manifolds with isomorphic intersection form are even stably diffeomorphic.

Since both the classification of smooth structures on 4-manifolds and the existence of [[Exotic sphere|exotic 4-spheres]] are important open problems in differential topology, it seems that a connection could exist using connected sums with exotic 4-spheres. However, if <math>\Sigma</math> is an exotic 4-sphere, then Wall's theorem on stabilization guarantees the existence of a natural number <math>n\in\mathbb{N}</math> and a diffeomorphism:
:<math>
\Sigma\#n(S^2\times S^2)
\cong S^4\#n(S^2\times S^2)
\cong n(S^2\times S^2),
</math>
meaning that the connected sum with <math>\Sigma</math> causes no change in the smooth structure.

== Wall's theorem on automorphisms ==
'''Wall's theorem on automorphisms''' claims, that for a symmetric [[Unimodular matrix|unimodular]] [[bilinear form]] <math>Q\colon\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{Z}^n\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}</math> with <math>\operatorname{rk}(Q)-|\sigma(Q)|\geq 4</math> and two elements <math>x,y\in\mathbb{Z}</math> with same divisibility, self-intersection <math>Q(x,x)=Q(y,y)</math> and type, there exists an automorphism <math>f\colon\mathbb{Z}^n\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}^n</math> with <math>f(x)=y</math>.<ref>Scorpan 05, p. 152</ref>

Divisibility is the largest integer able to divide the element. Type refers to whether the element is characteristic or not. <math>\operatorname{rk}(Q)-|\sigma(Q)|</math> is always even, hence the above condition only excludes definite forms with <math>\operatorname{rk}(Q)-|\sigma(Q)|=0</math> and near-definite forms with <math>\operatorname{rk}(Q)-|\sigma(Q)|=2</math>. According to [[Serre classification|Serre's classification]], this includes only the hyperbolic form <math>H=Q_{S^2\times S^2}
=\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 1 \\
1 & 0
\end{pmatrix}</math> as well as <math>[+1]\oplus n[-1]</math> and <math>n[+1]\oplus[-1]</math>.

== Wall's theorem on diffeomorphisms ==
'''Wall's theorem on diffeomorphisms''' claims, that for a simply connected smooth 4-manifold <math>M</math> with [[Indefinite matrix|indefinite]] [[Intersection form of a 4-manifold|intersection form]] <math>Q_M</math>, every [[automorphism]] of <math>Q_{M\#(S^2\times S^2)}
\cong Q_M\oplus H</math> (with the hyperbolic form <math>H=Q_{S^2\times S^2}
=\begin{pmatrix}
0 & 1 \\
1 & 0
\end{pmatrix}</math>) comes from a self-[[diffeomorphism]] on <math>M\#(S^2\times S^2)</math>.<ref name=":0">Scorpan 05, p. 153</ref> This shows an important difference between smooth and [[Topological manifold|topological]] 4-manifolds since the latter require no stabilization. For a simply connected topological 4-manifold <math>M</math> with indefinite intersection form <math>Q_M</math>, every automorphism of <math>Q_M</math> comes from a self-[[homeomorphism]] on <math>M</math>.<ref name=":0" />
